thesis: This engine cannot express relative strength -- entry and exit are evaluated per symbol against that symbol's own bars, with no cross-sectional comparison, so there is no way to buy 'the strongest sector' or trade a spread. What this card does is apply one absolute condition -- close above its own 50-day average with RSI(14) between 55 and 80, a confirmed non-extreme uptrend -- identically across 12 names, one per GICS sector (two in Consumer Discretionary, for reasons given below), and cap concurrent holdings at 4 of 12. That cap plus the universe's fill order is the only 'rotation' logic available. The prior semis rotation card (A-rotation) ran this exact entry/exit/stop/target/hold-day logic against 9 correlated chip names (mean pairwise correlation 0.589) and called the result a concentrated sector bet, not a rotation. This card changes exactly one variable -- the universe's correlation structure -- to test whether breadth itself is worth anything: XOM (Energy), CAT (Industrials), HD and MCD (Consumer Discretionary, housing vs. restaurant spend), KO (Staples), JNJ (Health Care), JPM (Financials), MSFT (Info Tech, no fab exposure), VZ (Communication Services), NEE (Utilities), LIN (Materials), PLD (Real Estate). Measured trailing-253-session pairwise correlation through 2026-02-13: mean 0.245, versus 0.589 for the incumbent semis book -- roughly 2.4x more diversified by this measure. Universe order is not alphabetical: names are ordered by ascending average correlation to the rest of the book (MSFT 0.12 lowest, LIN 0.36 highest), so when more than 4 names qualify on the same session -- which happens on about 71% of sessions in the trailing two years -- the broker's fixed fill order fills the most-diversifying names first, the one ordering rule available that is actually about breadth rather than an arbitrary tiebreak. Selection is not index-derived: these names were chosen and ordered by measured correlation structure and liquidity, not by picking 'the largest member of each sector' off today's constituent list, so the card is not subject to the universe_knowable_from gate on that basis -- though every name here is, in fact, a company that survived to be listed today, and that is a real limit on what this backtest can show, stated plainly rather than hidden. On the other side of these trades: momentum/trend traders across multiple unrelated sectors who already positioned before this rule confirms; mean-reversion sellers fading strength inside a still-intact uptrend in any one of these sectors; and the fact that a rule this permissive, when it fires on names in 8+ different sectors at once, describes 'the market is going up,' not a sector call -- in which case this basket simply behaves like a slow, capped SPY substitute, and diversification purchased no edge, only lower variance.
entry: close > sma(50) and rsi(14) > 55 and rsi(14) < 80
